children: American Bitcoin Corp. has lined up a $150 million committed revolving credit facility with FalconX. The loan is backed by some of the company's Bitcoin.

The agreement was signed on November 18, 2026, through the Nasdaq-listed company's subsidiary, American Bitcoin Operating LLC. The lender is FalconX Charlie, Inc., an entity tied to the digital asset brokerage FalconX.
As of the November 23 announcement, American Bitcoin had not drawn anything from the line. The money is set aside for general corporate purposes and strategic growth.
Borrowing costs a loan fee of 5.95% per annum. There's also a commitment fee on any undrawn amounts, which is the price of keeping the door open even when nobody walks through it.

The facility runs for an initial two-year term, maturing on November 18, 2028. It includes options for up to three extensions, giving the company room to keep the arrangement alive past that date if both sides agree.
The collateral sits in custody at Anchorage Digital Bank N.A., a federally chartered crypto bank.
The facility uses three thresholds to manage risk. The initial coverage ratio is set at 143%, the maintenance trigger at 130%, and the default threshold at 105%.

Put simply, American Bitcoin has to pledge about $1.43 in Bitcoin for every dollar it borrows. If Bitcoin's price slides and that cushion shrinks to $1.30, the company will need to top up its collateral or otherwise shore up the position.
If the cushion falls all the way to $1.05 per dollar owed, the loan hits default territory.
The credit line lands shortly after American Bitcoin said its reserves had surpassed 8,500 BTC. That compares with 8,427 BTC as of September 30, 2026.
The company is majority-owned by Hut 8, the Bitcoin miner. It was co-founded by Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr.
FalconX has previously arranged Bitcoin-backed financing for other firms.

The biggest selling point is that the facility is non-dilutive. Raising money by issuing new shares shrinks existing shareholders' slice of the company, while borrowing against assets leaves ownership untouched.
The 5.95% loan fee is the other piece of the calculus. Any money drawn needs to generate returns, through mining expansion or other growth, that justify paying that rate on top of the commitment fee.

Because nothing has been drawn yet, the facility currently works more like an insurance policy than a loan. It gives management a ready source of liquidity if an opportunity, or an emergency, shows up.

title: American Bitcoin secures $150M credit line from FalconX
